findings.claim: The paper still says gate's max_token_budget is the site's spend ceiling. The text is unmarked, so the paper contradicts N15 and its own §4.8 revision. The same stale line is copied into the assembled agent-led-site.md.
findings.evidence: 04-architecture.md:240 (list 'Site server to UAR (PLANNED, Phase 0)', not marked superseded): "Gate's `max_token_budget` hook and a per-credential rate limit on the site identity are the site's spend ceiling (§4.8)." §4.8 at 04-architecture.md:347-352 says the opposite: "an earlier version made gate's `max_token_budget` the ceiling; that design is superseded" and "Gate is optional". The B6 done-when grep (`ceiling at flint-gate|ceiling is flint-gate|ceiling is flint-gate's`) cannot match this wording, so B6's own check passes while the defect stays. Acceptance criterion 4: no leftover section may still make flint-gate the enforcing spend ceiling.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite line 240: the site server's reserve-and-settle meter is the ceiling (§4.8); gate's budget is optional (D-4); the per-credential rate limit can still apply. Reassemble agent-led-site.md. Replace the B6 grep with one that also matches `max_token_budget.*spend ceiling`.

findings.claim: The deployed FR-8 check was moved into site-agent-seed 1.3, but the old 'Depends on' edges were never updated, so the dependency graph now has a cycle and no longer matches A3.
findings.evidence: site-agent-seed/tasks.md:5 says 1.3 "also holds the **deployed** FR-8 chunk check", which needs the stack deployed (k8s-stack-manifests, then github-deploy-workflows). But k8s-stack-manifests/proposal.md:9 still reads "Depends on: ... `site-agent-seed`, `site-chat-proxy`", and site-chat-proxy/proposal.md:9 still reads "Depends on: `local-compose-stack`, `site-agent-seed`". In A3, site-chat-proxy is in step 2 (before the first deploy) and site-agent-seed is in step 6 (after kb-chunking-quality and gate-site-credentials). The edges A3 adds are also missing from the proposals: github-deploy-workflows/proposal.md:9 lacks `ci-secrets-out`; k8s-stack-manifests/proposal.md:9 lacks `uar-runtime-host-lockdown`; site-agent-seed/proposal.md:9 lacks `kb-chunking-quality` and `gate-site-credentials`. Plan review round 2 judged this 'one direction, no cycle', but it checked only the N9 to site-agent-seed edge.
findings.suggested_fix: Split site-agent-seed: a local gate (1.3), and a separate deployed FR-8 check task, or a separate change, that runs after github-deploy-workflows. Update the 'Depends on' lines in all four existing proposals to match A3.

findings.claim: The claim that the meter 'can never overshoot' is unsupported. Settlement to the actual usage.total_tokens is unconditional and has no cap, and nothing proves a run's total_tokens stays at or below the reserved max_tokens_per_turn.
findings.evidence: Child plan.md:61 says "the budget can never be overshot"; site-spend-ceiling/proposal.md:7 says "concurrent turns cannot overshoot". Task 1.3 settles to `usage.total_tokens` with no condition. Task 1.8 only asks to 'set max_tokens_per_turn so a reservation covers the largest turn'. UAR's run-scope token limit is checked when each model attempt is admitted (`cost_budget.rs` check_limits: `tokens + reserved >= limit` then bail). It does not cap the tokens of the attempt already running, so a multi-step run (KB retrieval, a tool loop) can report total_tokens above the limit. The plan's Risks section asks for 'an atomic conditional update ... per settlement', but no task specifies settlement semantics. Done-when (3) tests only concurrent reservations, so it cannot catch an overshoot during settlement. Task 1.4 also asks for daily and monthly in 'the same atomic reservation', which one `UPDATE ... WHERE` on one row cannot do without a transaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify settlement: one atomic update that adds (actual - reserved). Define behaviour when actual > reserved: record the overshoot, alert, and bound it by documenting the UAR per-turn cap. Use a SurrealDB transaction for the daily and monthly rows together. Add a done-when case: a run whose usage exceeds its reservation, and the total afterwards.

findings.claim: Task 1.2 refuses any turn whose conditional UPDATE matches no row. No task creates the daily or monthly counter row, so as written the meter refuses every turn at each day and month rollover.
findings.evidence: 1.2: "run the single atomic `UPDATE … SET total += n WHERE total + n <= budget` ... If no row is updated, refuse the turn with the offline state." No task in 1.1-1.12 creates or upserts a per-day or per-month record, or defines how a period key such as the date is chosen, so the first turn of each period updates zero rows. The plan and spec carry the same single-statement wording (spec.md:4, 09-implementation-plan.md:50).
findings.suggested_fix: Define the period key and create the row (an UPSERT, or a transaction that creates the row at total 0 when missing) before the conditional update. Add a rollover case to done-when.

findings.claim: Done-when (5) cannot tell a fail-closed meter from a fail-open one. The production SurrealDB that test (5) stops is the same instance UAR runs on, and the task's pass condition doesn't require 'no upstream call'.
findings.evidence: 1.12(5): "with SurrealDB stopped, turns are refused". The meter lives on the same StatefulSet as UAR's ns=uar (k8s/base/surrealdb-statefulset.yaml, replicas: 1), so stopping it also breaks UAR. A fail-open meter would forward the turn, UAR would fail, and the visitor would still see a refusal. Only spec.md:32 adds "and no upstream call is made"; the task omits it. site-chat-offline-states/tasks.md 1.9 has the same flaw ("stop SurrealDB → offline notice"). The child plan (line 179) also says the six tests must pass 'on the deployed stack', and D-1 means that is production. Task 1.12 names no environment, and stopping production SurrealDB is a destructive action with no confirmation step.
findings.suggested_fix: Make (5) assert that UAR receives no request (UAR request log or counter) or block only the meter's connection (NetworkPolicy or credential revocation) instead of stopping SurrealDB. State the environment for 1.12, and add an operator confirmation step for any production outage test.

findings.claim: With D-2 recorded as an accepted risk and U12 open, §6.4 item 3 can never get its evidence. Phase 0 exit then either can't be reached, or will be passed by counting the accepted risk as evidence, which in effect closes U12. Neither the plan nor the paper says which.
findings.evidence: 09:88 exit criterion: "Every §6.4 item from 1 to 18 has evidence filed in the change mapped to it above." 09:69 maps item 3 to "Operator, D-2 ... neither exit was taken, so U12 stays open". 06-security-privacy.md:89 item 3 still requires written confirmation or a capped pay-as-you-go key. 01-whitepaper.md:94: "Until the operator has written confirmation ... the site cannot launch its agent." The child plan's D-2 row covers only kill criterion 1 and the spend alert, not this exit criterion.
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly that §6.4 item 3 is either (a) excluded from Phase 0 exit as an operator-accepted risk, and say what is filed in its place, or (b) still blocking, so Phase 0 cannot exit until an exit route is taken. Record the choice in the decision log.

findings.claim: A3 puts the first deploy before the spend ceiling and kill switch. The production stack, reachable by anyone who sends a Host header, will make paid model calls with no global ceiling and no kill switch until step 7 lands.
findings.evidence: Parent plan Order: step 6 'Deploy path' (E10, E11, E7), then step 7 'On the deployed stack: N15 ...'. The kill switch is a task of site-spend-ceiling (1.9). 09-implementation-plan.md:15 admits "Not public does not mean unreachable: anyone who sends `Host: know-me.tools` to the gateway reaches the deployment." 06-security-privacy.md T1: the per-IP limiter is per replica and in memory, and "A botnet of N IPs gets N times the quota." Combined with D-2 (Token Plan, with suspension risk), the window between the first deploy and N15 has no global cap. The plan names no failure scenario for that window and accepts no risk for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Either land the kill switch, and a minimal fail-closed meter or the knowme-web route held at 0 replicas, before the first deploy, or record this window as an operator-accepted risk with a bound (duration, provider-side alert in place first).
